passages.title: Passage 1 — Reporting hazards
passages.text: Every worker on a jobsite shares __1__ for safety. A hazard that one person notices but does not report can easily __2__ a coworker hours later. For that reason most contractors require unsafe conditions to be written up __3__ they are found, rather than at the end of the shift. Workers who speak up are not being difficult; they are __4__ the standard that keeps the whole crew healthy and working. Over time, a crew that treats reporting as routine builds a __5__ in which small problems get corrected before they turn into injuries.

passages.title: Passage 2 — How an apprenticeship works
passages.text: An apprenticeship differs from a traditional college program because it pairs paid work with __6__ instruction. Apprentices earn wages from the first day, and their pay rises as they __7__ each measurable skill level. Employers value the model because graduates arrive already __8__ to the pace and the expectations of the trade. The arrangement also demands real __9__ from the apprentice: attendance, punctuality and steady effort are judged just as closely as test scores. Those who treat the program as a multi-year __10__ rather than a temporary job tend to advance fastest.

passages.title: Passage 3 — Friction and heat
passages.text: Whenever two surfaces slide across one another, friction __11__ some of the energy of motion into heat. Engineers cannot remove friction completely, so they __12__ it instead, using lubricants, bearings and carefully chosen materials. A bearing that runs dry will overheat quickly, __13__ the metal to expand and bind. __14__, a properly lubricated bearing can run for years with very little wear.

passages.title: Passage 4 — Hydraulic systems
passages.text: A hydraulic system transmits force through a confined __15__. Because liquids are very nearly incompressible, pressure applied at one point is __16__ equally in every direction. This lets a small force on a small piston lift a heavy load on a larger piston, provided the smaller piston travels a __17__ distance. Air trapped in the lines compresses under load and makes the controls feel spongy, so a technician must __18__ the system after any repair. Fluid levels should also be checked __19__, because a slow leak can go unnoticed until performance drops off.

passages.title: Passage 5 — Talking through the work
passages.text: Clear communication prevents more accidents than any single piece of equipment. When a mechanic gives a helper a task, the helper should repeat it back so that any __20__ is caught right away. Vague phrases such as “over there” or “in a minute” leave far too much room for __21__. Written notes carry the further __22__ of leaving a record the next shift can read. Crews that communicate well waste less material, finish sooner and __23__ fewer callbacks.

passages.title: Passage 6 — Codes and inspections
passages.text: Elevator equipment is governed by codes revised on a regular __24__. An installation that met every requirement ten years ago may no longer be __25__ today, and an inspector is obliged to cite it. Rather than treating the updates as a nuisance, experienced mechanics read them as a __26__ of lessons learned from past failures. Keeping a current copy of the applicable code on hand is therefore __27__ for anyone who signs off on work.

passages.title: Passage 7 — Circuits
passages.text: Current flows through a circuit only when the path is __28__. Opening a switch creates a gap and the current stops. Resistance __29__ the flow of current, and the energy spent overcoming it shows up as heat in the conductor. A conductor too small for its load will therefore run hot, which is why wire is __30__ according to the current it has to carry. Before working on any circuit a technician confirms it is de-energized, because a meter reading is far more reliable than an __31__.

questions.stem: Although the replacement part arrived late, the crew was able to ______ the schedule by working through the afternoon.
questions.explanation: After “able to” an English verb takes its base form: able to recover.

questions.stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is maintenance: main-ten-ance.

questions.stem: Neither of the two hoistway doors ______ properly aligned.
questions.explanation: Neither is singular, so it takes the singular verb was. The phrase “of the two doors” does not change that.

questions.stem: The supervisor's instructions were concise. Concise most nearly means:
questions.explanation: Concise means saying much in few words — brief and clear.

questions.stem: Gear A turns clockwise, as the arrow shows. Which way does gear B turn?
questions.explanation: Meshed gears always turn in opposite directions. Where the teeth touch, one gear's teeth push the other's the other way.

questions.stem: Gear A has 10 teeth and drives gear B, which has 30 teeth. Gear B turns:
choices: At the same speed as gear A
questions.explanation: The larger gear needs three of A's turns to complete one of its own, so it turns a third as fast. Bigger gear, slower speed.

questions.stem: Gear A turns clockwise. Which way does gear C turn?
questions.explanation: Each mesh reverses direction. A clockwise makes B counterclockwise, which makes C clockwise again. Odd-numbered gears match the first.

questions.stem: Pulley A drives pulley B through an ordinary uncrossed belt. Pulley A turns clockwise. Which way does B turn?
questions.explanation: A straight belt carries motion without reversing it, so both pulleys turn the same way.

questions.stem: The same two pulleys are now connected by a crossed belt. Pulley A turns clockwise. Which way does B turn?
questions.explanation: Crossing the belt swaps which side of each pulley the belt pulls on, so the driven pulley turns the opposite way.

questions.stem: A large pulley drives a small pulley by a belt. The small pulley turns:
choices: At the same speed as the driver
questions.explanation: The belt moves at one speed, and the small pulley has less distance around it, so it must spin more times to keep up.

questions.stem: A 100 lb load hangs from a single fixed pulley bolted to the ceiling. About how much force is needed to lift it?
questions.explanation: A fixed pulley only changes the direction of your pull. It gives no mechanical advantage, so you still pull the full 100 lb.

questions.stem: The same 100 lb load now hangs from a movable pulley. About how much force is needed to lift it?
questions.explanation: Two rope sections support the load, so each carries half the weight and you pull about 50 lb — but you pull twice as much rope.

questions.stem: A block and tackle has four rope sections supporting the load. About how much force lifts the 200 lb load?
questions.explanation: Count the rope sections holding the load. Four sections share 200 lb, so each carries 50 lb and that is what you pull.

questions.stem: Both ropes are pulled in at the same speed. Which system raises its box faster?
choices: Both rise at the same speed
questions.explanation: In A the box rises as fast as the rope moves. In B the rope splits between two sections, so the box rises only half as fast — the trade for the easier pull.

questions.stem: A 60 lb weight sits 3 ft from the fulcrum. What weight 2 ft out on the other side will balance the bar?
questions.explanation: Weight times distance must match on both sides. 60 × 3 = 180, and 180 ÷ 2 = 90 lb.

questions.stem: You are prying up the load with a bar. Which fulcrum position makes the lift easiest?
choices: Position B, close to your hands
Position A, close to the load
Neither; the effort is the same
questions.explanation: The closer the fulcrum sits to the load, the longer the effort arm and the greater the advantage. Put the fulcrum near what you are lifting.

questions.stem: The load in the wheelbarrow is shifted forward, closer to the wheel. Lifting the handles becomes:
questions.explanation: The wheel is the fulcrum. Moving the load toward it shortens the load's arm, so less effort is needed at the handles.

questions.stem: Two workers carry a plank with a load resting nearer worker A. Who carries more of the weight?
questions.explanation: The nearer end of a carried load always takes the larger share. Move the load to the middle and they split it evenly.

questions.stem: Two ramps reach the same height. Which takes less force to push a heavy barrel up?
questions.explanation: A longer ramp is less steep, so the same height is gained over more distance and less force is needed at each moment.

questions.stem: Two ladders lean against a wall. Which is more likely to slip out at the bottom?
choices: Both are equally likely to slip
questions.explanation: The flatter the ladder, the harder it pushes outward along the floor, and friction at the base has more to fight. Steeper is more secure.

questions.stem: Two containers weigh the same. Which tips over more easily if the floor is bumped?
choices: Both tip at the same point
questions.explanation: A tall narrow box has a high center of gravity and a small base, so a small tilt puts its weight past the edge.

questions.stem: A 20 lb force presses on the small piston. About how much force does the large piston deliver?
questions.explanation: Pressure is the same throughout the fluid: 20 lb on 1 sq in is 20 psi. Acting on 10 sq in, that gives 20 × 10 = 200 lb.

questions.stem: In that same hydraulic jack, the large piston moves:
choices: Exactly as far as the small piston
questions.explanation: You never get something for nothing. The force is multiplied ten times, so the distance is cut to a tenth.

questions.stem: Both tanks are filled with water to the same depth. The water pressure at the bottom is:
questions.explanation: Pressure in a liquid depends only on depth, not on how much water sits above. Same depth means same pressure at the bottom.

questions.stem: Setup B hangs the same 50 lb load from two identical springs side by side. Compared with setup A, the springs in B:
questions.explanation: Two springs side by side each carry only 25 lb, so each stretches half as far as the single spring carrying the whole load.

questions.stem: Setup B hangs the same 50 lb load from two identical springs joined end to end. Compared with setup A, the load in B hangs:
choices: Higher, because the springs stretch less in total
Lower, because the springs stretch more in total
questions.explanation: Springs end to end each feel the full 50 lb, so each stretches the full amount and the stretches add up.

questions.stem: A 10 lb weight stretches this spring 2 inches. If a 20 lb weight is hung on it instead, the spring stretches about:
questions.explanation: A spring stretches in proportion to the pull. Double the weight, double the stretch: 4 inches.

questions.stem: The round gear turns clockwise against the toothed bar below it. Which way does the bar slide?
questions.explanation: Look at the bottom of the gear, where the teeth meet the bar. On a clockwise gear the bottom travels left, dragging the bar left with it.

questions.stem: The rope you pull is wrapped around the large outer wheel; the load hangs from the small inner axle. Making the outer wheel larger gives:
choices: More lifting force for the same effort
Less lifting force for the same effort
questions.explanation: A bigger wheel means a longer lever arm for your pull against the same axle, so the advantage grows — at the cost of pulling more rope.

questions.stem: Both wrenches fit the same stubborn nut. Which loosens it with less effort from your hand?
questions.explanation: Turning force is your push multiplied by the handle length. A longer handle produces more torque from the same hand force.

questions.stem: Compared with the coarse screw, one full turn of the fine-threaded screw drives it:
choices: A shorter distance into the material
A longer distance into the material
questions.explanation: Threads closer together advance less per turn. That is why fine threads turn more easily but need more turns.

questions.stem: The two blocks are identical. Which needs more force to start sliding?
choices: Block B, on the smooth surface
Block A, on the rough surface
questions.explanation: A rougher surface produces more friction, and friction is what your push has to overcome before the block moves.

questions.stem: Two pendulums are released together. Pendulum A, the longer one:
choices: Swings back and forth more slowly
Swings back and forth more quickly
Swings at exactly the same rate as B
questions.explanation: A longer pendulum takes longer to complete each swing. Its weight does not matter — only its length.

questions.stem: These two gears are meshed and running. Which one delivers more turning force at its shaft?
choices: Both deliver the same turning force
questions.explanation: Gears trade speed for force. The large gear turns slower, and what it gives up in speed it gains in torque.

questions.stem: Sprocket A drives sprocket B through a chain. Sprocket A turns counterclockwise. Which way does B turn?
questions.explanation: A chain runs like an uncrossed belt and does not reverse anything, so both sprockets turn the same way.

questions.stem: The oval cam turns on its shaft and pushes the follower rod up and down. In one full turn of the cam, the follower rises:
choices: It does not rise at all
questions.explanation: An oval has two long sides. Each one sweeps past the follower in a single revolution, so the follower is pushed up twice per turn.

questions.stem: As the tank fills, the float rises and swings the lever. The valve:
choices: Closes, slowing or stopping the flow
Opens further, speeding up the flow
questions.explanation: That is the point of a float valve: rising water lifts the float, the lever pushes the valve shut, and the tank stops filling.

questions.stem: Water flows steadily through this pipe. In the narrow section the water moves:
choices: At the same speed as in the wide section
Slower than in the wide section
Faster than in the wide section
questions.explanation: The same amount of water must pass every second. Squeezed into a smaller opening, it has to travel faster.

questions.stem: The same 100 lb load is hung two ways. In which setup is each rope under more tension?
choices: Setup A, with the ropes nearly vertical
The tension is the same in both
Setup B, with the ropes spread wide
questions.explanation: Spread ropes pull mostly sideways against each other, so only part of each rope's pull holds the weight up. The wider the angle, the higher the tension.

2¾ ÷ ½ =

questions.stem: A crew installs 3 elevators in 12 days. Working at the same rate, how many days will 7 elevators take?
questions.explanation: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 days each, and 4 × 7 = 28 days.

questions.stem: A motor turns at 1,200 rpm and drives a machine through a 3:1 speed reduction. The machine turns at:
questions.explanation: A 3:1 reduction divides the speed by 3: 1,200 ÷ 3 = 400 rpm.

questions.stem: What is the area of a rectangle 8.5 ft by 6 ft?
questions.explanation: Area is length × width: 8.5 × 6 = 51 sq ft.

A part's cost rises from $80 to $100. That is an increase of:
questions.explanation: The increase is $20 measured against the original $80: 20 ÷ 80 = 25%.

questions.explanation: Move both decimals two places: 60 ÷ 2 = 30.

questions.explanation: Multiply both sides by 6: x = 27. That is not offered, so the answer is No answer.

questions.stem: A 240-gallon tank fills at 15 gallons per minute. How long does it take to fill?
questions.explanation: 240 ÷ 15 = 16 minutes.

questions.stem: How many inches are in 3 ft 6 in?
questions.explanation: 3 × 12 = 36, plus 6 = 42 inches.

questions.stem: Pressure equals force divided by area (P = F ÷ A). If F = 180 lb and A = 9 sq in, then P equals:
questions.explanation: 180 ÷ 9 = 20 pounds per square inch.
